title: I'm making a Fallout-like RPG with AI – looking for feedback!
author: No_Piano_1857
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I'm currently developing a Fallout-like isometric RPG inspired by the classic Fallout games. My goal is to recreate the atmosphere, exploration, and role-playing freedom that made those games so memorable, while introducing AI-powered systems to make NPC interactions and the world feel more dynamic.

The game is still in development, and I'd really appreciate your honest feedback. If you're a fan of classic Fallout-style RPGs, I'd love to know what you think!

​

Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4546490/Arkansas\_2125/

Thanks for checking it out! Feel free to ask me anything about the game or its development.

replies.author: No_Piano_1857

replies.author: Desperate_Sale_4206

And I don't choose the first one that comes along because, as usual, some of you simplify me, seeing me as a nerd who mindlessly makes a copy-paste game. Tell me why I'm making this game for two years and not one. If I did it the way you think, I could have made it in a year.I am asking some of you to please not judge without asking how it is done. comments.author: bluesmaker
comments.body:
"Play as Thomas, a lone wanderer seeking the legendary Farm Restorer." 

I think you should not make the plot this similar to fallout. For a close copy to work you'd need to be satirizing fallout. But as far as I can tell, you're not doing that. Like "farm restorer" reads like a really uninspired ripoff of the G.E.C.K., which is an actually interesting name.

I would suggest you rethink the plot. If you just closely follow fallout, I think you're setting people up for disappointment.

replies.author: No_Piano_1857
replies.body: The plot is a mix of various Fallout elements. Once you play for a while (I recommend spending $5, it's really cheap), you'll see many differences between my plot and Fallout 2's. In Fallout, the GECK is a device that creates villages, for me it only restores crops. Agricultural tool because there is famine in the state of Arkansas and the villages are already there.

replies.body: This is unity, sorry, I forgot to write, and it is not created on tiles. Yes, these are 3D models and a well-positioned orthographic camera. This is not the technology from Fallout 1 and 2, this is technology that they could only dream about because players had weak computers back then. Today, where everyone has a computer capable of graphics, I used 3D models. The models aren't created in AI, which I regret because it's expensive and the model meshes aren't optimized. I use AI for textures and I also created one model of a shop refrigerator based on reference drawings created by AI.I think 2.5d is able to generate, just give a good prompt
